paper.title: The (Marginal) Value of a Search Ad: An Online Causal Framework for Repeated Second-price Auctions

settings.name_in_paper: Repeated second-price auctions with treatment-effect ad value, binary feedback
unmapped: Bids b in [0,1] in a second-price auction; reward = 1[b>=m_t](v_{t,1}-m_t) + 1[b<m_t]v_{t,0}
Ad value is a treatment effect Delta v_t = v_{t,1}-v_{t,0} which is never observed; only the realized outcome of the chosen treatment is observed
Linear model E[Delta v_t] = theta_*^T x_t with ||theta_*||_2 <= 1, ||x_t||_2 <= 1
Binary win/loss feedback, plus the highest other bid m_t revealed via payment only when winning (one-sided feedback)
Highest other bid i.i.d. from unknown CDF G that is (omega, lambda)-locally-bounded
The learner knows the HOB local-boundedness constants (omega, lambda)
Context sequence is oblivious (values independent over time conditioned on contexts)
settings.definition_quote: Consider a single bidder who jointly estimates the unknown (marginal) value and bids in repeated SPAs over a horizon of length $T$. A feature vector $x_t\in\R^d$ is revealed ... We consider \textit{binary feedback} where the bidder observes no additional information other than the win-loss indicator. ... the bidder observes the HOB $m_t$ from the payment rule if and only if she wins

settings.name_in_paper: Repeated second-price auctions with treatment-effect ad value (lower bound, full-information HOB, known G)
unmapped: Bids b in [0,1] in a second-price auction with treatment-effect value; linear model E[Delta v_t] = theta_*^T x_t, ||theta_*|| <= 1
Lower bound holds even if the HOB CDF G is perfectly known and the HOB is always observed; the treatment value itself is observed only through the realized outcome
settings.definition_quote: Even if the CDF $G$ is perfectly known, when $T\ge d^2$, it holds that $\reg^* = \Omega\parr{\sqrt{dT}}$. ... Since Theorem \ref{thm:main_lower} holds even under full-information HOB feedback

algorithms.name: Master routine (Algorithm 3) with UCB computation routine and better-of-two-UCBs selection

conditions: Assumption 1: E[Delta v_t] = theta_*^T x_t with ||theta_*||_2 <= 1
Assumption 2: HOB i.i.d. with (omega,lambda)-locally-bounded CDF, omega, lambda in (0,1) known
tuning: T_0 = ceil(sqrt(T) log T) initial rounds bidding 1

source.label: thm:main_upper
source.quote: Suppose Assumption \ref{assum:linear_model}--\ref{assum:oblivious} hold. Under this binary feedback, there is a bidding algorithm $\pi$ that achieves \[ \reg(\pi) = O\parr{\sqrt{dT}\log^3 T + d\log^5T}. \]

results.notes: Regret defined through expected payoffs r̄_t against per-round optimal bid, so pseudo-regret. Feedback mapped to partial_monitoring (censored win/loss with payment revealed on winning). Table 1 notes the same upper bound under full-information.

conditions: holds even under full-information HOB feedback
hard instance: v_{t,0} = 0, v_{t,1} Bernoulli, HOB = 1/2 Unif[0,1] + 1/2 point mass

source.label: thm:main_lower
source.quote: Suppose Assumption \ref{assum:linear_model}--\ref{assum:oblivious} hold. Even if the CDF $G$ is perfectly known, when $T\ge d^2$, it holds that \[ \reg^* = \Omega\parr{\sqrt{dT}}. \]

results.notes: Minimax lower bound over (G, theta_*). Proof embeds d-1 independent two-point instances from Theorem 3 (non-contextual Omega(sqrt T) bound).
